heard: Four interacting galaxies share the sky with a supersonic imposter. Discovered in 1877 by Edouard Steffen, this group in Pegasus looks like a tight squad. Modern telescopes revealed that the brightest member, NGC 7320, is actually a foreground interloper. It sits just 39 million light years away, while the other four are parked much further out. Another intruder named NGC 7318B is currently plowing straight into the group. This supersonic impact generates a colossal shock wave bigger than the entire Milky Way. Even Hollywood used the group to represent glowing angels in the holiday classic, It's a Wonderful Life. Four interacting galaxies share the sky with a supersonic imposter.
